title: Holy Scripture - WCF Chapter 1 (sections 1-3)
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: Introduction to the Series and Confession
subpoints: Plan to study WCF Chapter 1 systematically for the first month
Importance of defining beliefs about Scripture before other doctrines

outline.title: General Revelation in Creation
subpoints: Creation manifests God's goodness, wisdom, and power
The 'light of nature' leaves man unexcusable
Universal knowledge of God's existence through nature

outline.title: The Insufficiency of General Revelation
subpoints: Creation is not sufficient for saving knowledge of God
Humanity suppresses the truth and darkens their hearts
The 'fool' continually denies God despite evident evidence

outline.title: The Necessity of Special Revelation
subpoints: God revealed Himself in sundry times and divers manners
Scripture committed to writing for preservation and comfort
Scripture is necessary against the corruption of flesh and malice of Satan

summary:
In this morning service, Pastor Tito Lyro introduces a new series on Psalm 119, which will span 23 lessons. To complement this study, the congregation will spend the first month examining Chapter 1 of the Westminster Confession of Faith (WCF), titled 'Of the Holy Scripture.' This systematic approach aims to establish a foundational understanding of what the Bible says about itself before delving into specific psalm texts.

The lesson focuses on WCF Section 1, which addresses the relationship between general and special revelation. It is taught that while the light of nature and the works of creation manifest God's goodness, wisdom, and power, they are insufficient to provide the knowledge of God necessary for salvation. Creation serves as a universal witness to God's existence, leaving all humanity without excuse, as supported by Romans 1:18-25 and Psalm 19. However, due to human depravity, individuals suppress this truth and worship creatures rather than the Creator.

Consequently, God pleased to reveal Himself in a special way through Scripture. This written revelation is necessary for the better preservation and propagation of truth, providing sure establishment and comfort to the church against the corruption of the flesh and the malice of Satan. The session emphasizes that while general revelation condemns the world, it is only through the special revelation of Scripture that saving knowledge is imparted.
